Staudhammer and LeMay (2000) DBH–height models for coastal British Columbia

Source: R/hd_staudhammerlemay2000.R
hd_staudhammerlemay2000.Rd

Vectorized implementation of the DBH–height models of Staudhammer and LeMay (2000) for western redcedar (THUJ.PLI), red alder (ALNU.RUB), Douglas-fir (PSEU.MEN) and western hemlock (TSUG.HET). Predicts total tree height (m) from DBH (cm) alone, or from DBH and stand-density measures.

Usage

hd_staudhammerlemay2000(
  DBH,
  species,
  variant = c("dbh", "density"),
  TPH = NULL,
  BA = NULL,
  DMAX = NULL,
  keep_model_id = FALSE
)

Arguments

DBH

Numeric vector. Tree level. Diameter at breast height (1.3 m), in cm. Must be >= 0. Only trees above 2 cm DBH were recorded (p. 304).

species

Character vector. Tree level. NFI species codes (e.g. "PSEU.MEN"; compact "PSEUMEN" is accepted). Supported: ALNU.RUB, PSEU.MEN, THUJ.PLI, TSUG.HET.

variant

Model variant: "dbh" (default; eq. 2) or "density" (eq. 2a for red alder, eq. 2b for the other species).

TPH

Optional numeric vector. Plot level. Stems per hectare, all species combined (source "TSTEMSHA", p. 304; trees with DBH > 2 cm, live or dead status not stated). Must be > 0. Required by variant = "density" for red alder.

BA

Optional numeric vector. Plot level. Basal area per hectare (m²/ha), all species combined (source "TBAHA", p. 304; same tree basis as TPH). Must be > 0. Required by variant = "density" for red alder.

DMAX

Optional numeric vector. Plot level. Maximum DBH (cm) of all trees on the plot, all species; used to compute the relative DBH (source "REL_dbh" = "dbh divided by the maximum dbh for all species", p. 304). Must be > 0 and >= DBH. Required by variant = "density" for western redcedar, Douglas-fir and western hemlock.

keep_model_id

Logical. If TRUE, add column model_id ("staudhammerlemay2000_dbh" or "staudhammerlemay2000_density").

Value

A tibble with column height (m) and, if keep_model_id = TRUE, model_id.

Details

Model scope: fitted to the 1995 inventory of the UBC Malcolm Knapp Research Forest (about 5000 ha, Coastal Western Hemlock zone, coastal BC): 327 plots in 82 clusters, heights measured on a subjectively chosen subset of 763 trees (p. 304). The source alder model ("D") combines Alnus rubra and A. tenuifolia; it is used here for red alder (ALNU.RUB) only. Alder had only 28 trees on 16 plots.

Model form (eq. 2, Yang et al. 1978; p. 305): $$H = 1.3 + E_1 [1 - \exp(E_2 \, DBH^{E_3})].$$ The intercept is constrained to 1.3 m at DBH = 0.

Variants (chosen with variant):

  • "dbh" (default): eq. 2, with \(E_1\), \(E_2\), \(E_3\) species constants (Table 5, p. 308). All four species.

  • "density": parameter prediction (Table 5, p. 308). For red alder (eq. 2a), \(E_k = c_{k0} + c_{k1} TPH + c_{k2} BA\). For western redcedar, Douglas-fir and western hemlock (eq. 2b), \(E_k = c_{k0} + c_{k1} R + c_{k2} R^2\), where \(R = DBH / DMAX\) is the tree's relative DBH. TPH and BA are required only when the data include red alder, and DMAX only when they include the other species.

Within a plot (fixed DMAX), eq. 2b heights increase with DBH up to a relative DBH of about 0.85–0.95 and then decrease slightly for the plot's largest trees; this follows from the published quadratic in \(R\). Predictors not used by the selected variant or species are ignored with a warning. Coefficients are ordinary nonlinear least-squares fits (SAS PROC NLIN); no calibration information is published.

Corrected coefficient: for western redcedar (eq. 2b), the slope of \(E_2\) on \(R^2\) is printed as 0.1551. With that value \(E_2\) becomes positive for \(R > 0.23\), giving negative heights (e.g. -47 m at DBH = 30 cm, \(R\) = 0.5), which is inconsistent with the reported fit (RMSE 4.308 m, Table 2). The value 0.01551 (a dropped zero) is used: it gives plausible heights and matches the DBH-only \(E_2\) at \(R = 1\). This correction is an inference, not a published erratum.

Validity: far outside the fitting data the "density" parameters can become invalid (\(E_1 \le 0\), \(E_2 \ge 0\) or \(E_3 \le 0\)): Douglas-fir with \(R < 0.062\), redcedar with \(R < 0.019\), hemlock with \(R < 0.008\), and red alder with TPH above about 7900 stems/ha or large BA with low TPH. Such rows raise an error; use variant = "dbh" for them. Inputs outside the per-species ranges of the fitting data (Table 1, p. 304: DBH, and for "density" also TPH, BA and \(R\)) are computed and reported in a single warning. Rows with NA in any used input return NA height. The source has no worked example, so the implementation is checked for plausibility only.

References

Staudhammer, C., and LeMay, V. (2000). Height prediction equations using diameter and stand density measures. The Forestry Chronicle, 76(2), 303–309. doi:10.5558/tfc76303-2

See also

hd_model_registry(), get_hd_model_info()

Examples

# DBH only (eq. 2)
hd_staudhammerlemay2000(
  DBH = c(10, 30, 60),
  species = c("PSEU.MEN", "TSUG.HET", "THUJ.PLI")
)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   9.44
#> 2  25.2 
#> 3  30.5 

# Stand density: relative DBH for conifers, stems/ha and basal area for alder
hd_staudhammerlemay2000(
  DBH = c(10, 30, 60, 15),
  species = c("PSEU.MEN", "TSUG.HET", "THUJ.PLI", "ALNU.RUB"),
  variant = "density",
  TPH = 1500, BA = 50, DMAX = 80,
  keep_model_id = TRUE
)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 2
#>   height model_id                    
#>    <dbl> <chr>                       
#> 1   2.99 staudhammerlemay2000_density
#> 2  29.3  staudhammerlemay2000_density
#> 3  29.7  staudhammerlemay2000_density
#> 4  18.1  staudhammerlemay2000_density

# Inside dplyr::mutate() with tree and plot data
trees <- data.frame(
  DBH = c(12, 45, 80),
  species = c("TSUG.HET", "PSEU.MEN", "PSEU.MEN"),
  DMAX = 80
)
dplyr::mutate(
  trees,
  hd_staudhammerlemay2000(DBH, species, variant = "density", DMAX = DMAX)
)
#>   DBH  species DMAX   height
#> 1  12 TSUG.HET   80 11.25201
#> 2  45 PSEU.MEN   80 31.01389
#> 3  80 PSEU.MEN   80 41.72672
